steps.intro: Feedback is a short written note from one person about another's work. This walkthrough only looks around — nothing is saved, and you can replay it any time from the "How feedback works" button.
steps.lifecycle: A feedback starts as Requested (someone asked for it) or as your own Draft, and reaches people only when it is Sent. A request can be Rejected, and a sent feedback can be Withdrawn.
steps.received: Received lists feedback others sent you. You never see a draft — only what has been sent.
steps.provided: Provided is everything you write: drafts, sent feedback, and requests waiting for you (status Requested). Open a request to pick it up or decline it.
steps.team: My team shows feedback about the people who report to you — only once it is sent. Drafts stay private to their author.
steps.teamScope: Under Filters, "Reports" switches between your direct reports and everyone below you. The other filters narrow by person, status and visibility.
steps.new: Writing feedback starts here. Let's open the form to look — nothing is saved until you press a save button.
steps.setup: Pick up to four recipients, then choose who may read it: Provider + subject keeps it between you, Public shows it on the Kudos wall.
steps.actions: Save draft keeps it private until you are ready; Save & send delivers it. You can still withdraw a sent feedback later.
steps.ask: Want feedback about yourself? On a person's card use "Ask for feedback" — they get a request in their Provided tab.
steps.request: As a manager you can also use "Request feedback for" on a report's card to ask someone else about them. You see that it exists, and read it once the provider sends it.
steps.kudos: Public, sent feedback appears on the Kudos wall for everyone. That's the whole flow — Done takes you back to Feedback.

steps.intro: A goal is something your manager sets for you and tracks over time. This walkthrough only looks around — nothing is saved, and you can replay it any time from the "How goals work" button.
steps.lifecycle: A goal starts as a Draft, goes live as Active, and ends as Archived with a summary. Every step can be reversed — an active goal can return to draft, and an archived one can be reopened.
steps.own: My goals lists every goal your managers set for you, drafts included. You see a goal from the moment it is created, not only once it is active.
steps.filters: Under Filters you narrow the list by title, status and creation date. The choice is remembered the next time you come back.
steps.progress: While a goal is Active, both you and your manager record progress: tick milestones on a Plan, or enter the current value on a Number or Percentage goal. An optional comment lands in the goal's history, and the other side is notified.
steps.managed: Goals I've set lists the goals you set for your reports. Under Filters, "Reports" widens it from your direct reports to everyone below you.
steps.new: Creating a goal starts here. Let's open the form to look — nothing is created until you press Create.
steps.definition: Pick the team member, give the goal a title, choose its kind — Plan with milestones, Number or Percentage with a target — and set a due date. A new goal always lands as a Draft.
steps.actions: Create saves the draft and then asks whether to activate it right away. We won't press it now — nothing is created in this walkthrough.
steps.manage: On a goal's page you run its lifecycle: Activate a draft, Return to draft an active goal, Archive it with a summary, or Reopen an archived one. Only the manager who set the goal can do this.
steps.subordinates: Each card on My subordinates has a Goals button listing what you set for that person, and New goal to add one. The card also counts their active goals.
steps.managers: Each card on My managers has a Goals button showing the goals that manager set for you, and counts the active ones. That's the whole flow — Done takes you back to Goals.
